correctness.rationale: Using Cauchy polytope projection, each of six equal-area triangular facets yields B_h(w,z)=sqrt(3)/2 sum_j max(h|e_j·w|,|z|/2). The six facet normal sign sums give maximum max(3sqrt(3)/4,sqrt(3)h). A nonzero absolute-linear form has its spherical minimum along a chamber extreme ray: for any nonparallel positive extreme-ray combination the Euclidean norm is smaller than its positive coefficient sum; the three pairwise facet-normal plane orbit types give candidate values 3h/2, sqrt(3)h/sqrt(1+h^2), and 9h/(4sqrt(1+3h^2)). Their squared differences switch at precisely 1/sqrt(3) and sqrt(11/21); the lower envelope is strictly increasing, while the upper envelope changes from constant to increasing at 3/4, proving the unique ratio optimum. Independently enumerated all 15 plane pairs and 64 signs across h=.3,.58,.72,.75,1,2, matching both bounds; continuum correctness comes from the finite-ray and exact monotonicity proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: The sharp three-phase transition and unique minimum over a natural full one-dimensional family of symmetric five-vertex polytopes quantify a classical geometric anisotropy measure, with exact optimizer/equality cases and potential use as a benchmark for projection-body optimization. This is not a renaming or tiny unmotivated numerical exception.

final_claim: For every symmetric equilateral-base triangular bipyramid of base circumradius one and positive apex height h, the minimum orthogonal-shadow area has three active-ray regimes with transitions h=1/sqrt(3) and sqrt(11/21); the maximum has two regimes switching at h=3/4; the unique minimum of the maximum/minimum area ratio is sqrt(129)/9 at h=3/4.
limitations: Only symmetric aligned equilateral-base triangular bipyramids; area extrema, not full shadow law; no universal shape-optimality statement.
